content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem: the root cause was the 09:16 deploy pointing the cache endpoint to port 6380 where nothing was listening, dropping cache hits to zero and spiking latency, confirmed by the rollback restoring baseline behavior. I need to flag that this confirmation is only correlational, since alternative hypotheses like broken code or a Redis outage weren't directly tested, and I should account for what the ClientDisconnected errors imply.

For the executive summary, I'm avoiding restating impact figures as if I computed them myself — I should reference the incident window (09:16–09:22 UTC) factually since that's part of the given data, but steer clear of quoting error-rate percentages or cost figures as my own conclusions. I'll keep the root cause explanation tight, just one or two sentences summarizing the cache misconfiguration and its effect.

assumptions: The cause is supported by correlation rather than direct proof: the change landed at the same minute the symptoms started, and reversing it restored baseline. No one independently verified the port configuration before and after the rollback.

The two alternative explanations - that the released code itself contained a broken cache client, or that the cache genuinely stopped listening at 09:16 for unrelated reasons - were never tested. The logs show connection refused from the cache, but the cache's own health was never checked, so an upstream outage coinciding with the deploy cannot be formally excluded.

The 'ClientDisconnected' account page errors run continuously from at least 08:46, well before onset, and are treated here as pre-existing background noise unrelated to this incident rather than as part of its impact.
Recovery is taken from the metrics returning to baseline at 09:22; the service was observed only briefly after the rollback, so durability of the fix beyond that point is assumed.
The user-visible effect is characterised as slow page loads based on the latency signal and the cache-miss path; no direct customer reports or session data were reviewed.
input.executive_summary: For roughly six minutes on the morning of 24 September 2026 (09:16 to 09:22 UTC), the shop's account pages became noticeably slow to load, and a small additional share of requests failed on top of the low level of failures the service normally sees. The cause was a routine change released at 09:16 that pointed the service at the wrong address for its fast-lookup store, so each page had to be assembled the slow way. Automated monitoring raised an alert at 09:21, the change was reversed within seconds of being identified, and normal speed returned by 09:22. Shoppers in that window would have experienced slow pages and, in a small number of cases, a failed page load; no data was lost and nothing required customer action. A draft code change has been opened to prevent the same misconfiguration from shipping again. The measured impact figures for the window are recorded separately in the incident record.
input.root_cause: A deploy to io-shop at 09:16 UTC (revision 0d8e826225f0de73958a8a8dd3d867b2ae249e72) pointed the summary cache at redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380, a port with no listener, so every cache lookup was refused and the cache hit ratio collapsed to zero. With no cache, all requests fell through to the slow path and p50 latency rose sharply until the configuration was rolled back at 09:21:39, after which the service returned to baseline at 09:22.
